overview: Synlait Milk is a New Zealand dairy processor based at Dunsandel, Canterbury, that manufactures infant formula and other advanced nutrition powders, dairy ingredients (whole/skim milk powder, cream, UHT products), and, through its Dairyworks subsidiary, consumer cheese and butter. Historically built around an exclusive manufacturing relationship with The a2 Milk Company, Synlait suffered a near-death solvency crisis in 2023-2024 and was recapitalised in September 2024 by China's state-linked Bright Dairy (now 65.25% owner) and a2 Milk (19.83%), leaving it a controlled, thinly-traded small-cap still working through a multi-year operational and balance-sheet recovery. In April 2026 it completed the sale of its loss-making North Island (Pokeno) assets to Abbott for ~NZ$307m, refocusing the group on its single Dunsandel (Canterbury) site.

business_model.summary: Synlait converts Canterbury (and, until April 2026, Waikato/North Island) farmer milk into higher-value nutritional powders, commodity dairy ingredients and consumer cheese/butter. Advanced Nutrition (infant formula/base powder, much of it manufactured for a2 Milk under a long-term supply agreement) has historically been the highest-margin segment; Ingredients (WMP/SMP, cream) is a lower-margin, commodity-price-exposed swing business used to absorb surplus milk; Consumer (Dairyworks: cheese, butter, private label) and Foodservice (UHT cream, mainly China/SE Asia) are smaller but growing and less volatile. Revenue is a mix of long-term contracted supply (a2 Milk, other nutrition customers), spot/contracted commodity ingredient sales, and branded/private-label consumer sales - not a subscription or purely recurring model, but the Advanced Nutrition base-powder contracts are multi-year and volume-committed.

revenue_streams.name: Advanced Nutrition (incl. a2 Milk base powder)
Ingredients (WMP/SMP/cream)
revenue_streams.trend: declining (volume down 25%, weak WMP pricing HY26)

revenue_streams.name: Consumer / Dairyworks (cheese, butter)
revenue_streams.trend: growing (+51% revenue HY26, Dairyworks core profit driver)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - a small number of large branded-nutrition and ingredients customers (a2 Milk, other infant-formula/nutrition brands) plus B2B/retail distribution for Dairyworks consumer brands (supermarkets/private label in NZ and Australia) and Foodservice customers in China/SE Asia
business_model.geographic_mix: By revenue destination HY26: New Zealand 54%, China 18% (up from 7% in HY25 as North Island Yashili-style China-label volumes wound down and Dunsandel-made product grew), Rest of Asia 16%, Australia 8%, Middle East/Africa 4%. Manufacturing is 100% New Zealand-based (Canterbury, South Island only, post the April 2026 North Island divestment).

main_competitors: Mataura Valley Milk (a2 Milk-owned, direct substitute for Synlait's a2 supply role)
Yashili/Mengniu and other China-facing infant-formula manufacturers
Bega Cheese and other consumer cheese/butter brands (Dairyworks' competitive set)
competitive_position.market_position: A small, specialist infant-formula and nutritional-powder contract manufacturer within a market Fonterra dominates by volume; historically valuable for its China SAMR-registered infant-formula manufacturing licences and its role as a2 Milk's primary contract manufacturer, but that exclusivity has now been dismantled and a2 Milk is building/acquiring alternative capacity (Mataura Valley Milk, the former Yashili Pokeno plant).

moat_factors.description: Dunsandel retains SAMR (China State Administration for Market Regulation) registration to manufacture China-label infant formula, a scarce, slow-to-obtain regulatory asset that is a real barrier to new entrants - but it is customer- and product-specific, not a durable Synlait-wide moat, and a2 Milk is diversifying its own registered capacity away from sole reliance on Synlait.

The historic exclusive Nutritional Products Manufacturing and Supply Agreement gave Synlait a captive, high-margin customer; a2 Milk cancelled exclusivity effective 1 Jan 2025 (settled for a NZ$25m payment to Synlait) while keeping minimum-volume and priority obligations in the NPMSA - so the relationship still matters but is no longer a lock-in.

moat_factors.factor: Grass-fed / Lead With Pride certification and traceability
moat_factors.description: MPI Grass-Fed accreditation and the Lead With Pride farm-assurance programme support premium positioning in China/Asia but are increasingly matched by competitors and are not unique to Synlait.

Sub-scale versus Fonterra; single-site (post North Island sale) Dunsandel manufacturing footprint limits flexibility and increases operating leverage to any one plant's performance, evidenced by the FY25-HY26 manufacturing-plan disruption.

weaknesses: Customer concentration: top three external customers were 36% of HY26 revenue (down from 55% in FY25, but still material) and a2 Milk historically represented a very large share of Advanced Nutrition earnings
Loss of a2 Milk manufacturing exclusivity removes the strongest structural advantage the business had
Single manufacturing site (Dunsandel) post the North Island sale concentrates operational risk
Commodity Ingredients segment has structurally thin/negative margins and is used as a milk-volume release valve, weighing on group profitability
History of manufacturing/quality execution failures (the FY25/HY26 'manufacturing plan adjustment' crisis) damages customer trust just as the company needs to rebuild it
Controlled company (Bright Dairy 65.25%) with a captive minority-shareholder register and thin free float, limiting independent governance leverage and NZX/ASX liquidity

growth_drivers: 'Stabilise, Simplify, Scale' recovery roadmap: Horizon 1 (stabilise operations/quality/balance sheet), Horizon 2 (simplify - cost-out, Palmerston North office closure saving >$2m/yr, right-sized revenue team), Horizon 3 (scale - new customers, new markets, new products)

North Island divestment to Abbott (completed 1 April 2026, ~NZ$307m gross, ~NZ$283m net after holdback) materially deleverages the balance sheet and removes a chronically loss-making CGU, freeing management focus on the single profitable-potential Dunsandel site

Dairyworks momentum: revenue +51% and gross profit +22% in HY26 on export growth (Thailand, Vietnam), private-label wins, and new products (Griffins snacking range, Burtfield & Co butter launch in the US via Foodstuffs, planned China retail test with Bright Dairy)
Foodservice UHT cream: China/SE Asia volumes +24%, turned from loss to profit in HY26; management targets doubling UHT cream volumes in FY27 and has expanded the Shanghai office/team

Advanced Nutrition diversification beyond a2 Milk: white-label supplement range targeting Asia-Pacific, customised early-life-nutrition trials for a Middle East customer, Nutrabase base-powder business development, and progressing a2 Milk's FDA infant-formula submission (a potential new US-bound revenue line)

Re-signed long-term Ingredients supply contracts with Synlait's two largest Ingredients customers (multi-year), and new Fixed Milk Price offering and secured milk premiums ($0.08-0.10/kgMS) intended to lock in Canterbury milk supply after the North Island farm exit
Post-divestment lower interest costs (bank facilities roughly halved from $400m to $200m using sale proceeds) should structurally improve underlying NPAT if operating performance normalises

business.risk: Customer concentration and a2 Milk relationship risk
business.description: a2 Milk remains Synlait's single most important customer and equity holder (19.83%), but has ended exclusivity, is building/acquiring its own manufacturing (Mataura Valley Milk, former Yashili Pokeno plant) and only retains minimum-volume/priority commitments under the NPMSA - a further reduction in a2 Milk volumes or a shift of China-label production elsewhere would be highly damaging

FY25-HY26 'manufacturing plan adjustments' directly caused an $80.6m NPAT loss and $183.4m operating cash outflow in HY26 alone; management concedes 'a series of challenges' (inventory shortfall, tactical milk sales, pivoting under pressure) and an ongoing insurance claim covers only part of the cost; repeated execution failures increase customer distrust at the exact time Synlait needs to rebuild inventory and reputation

business.risk: Single-site concentration post North Island sale
business.description: With Pokeno divested, all manufacturing is now concentrated at Dunsandel, removing site diversification and raising the stakes of any future production disruption

CEO Richard Wyeth resigned in May 2026 after only ~11 months in the role (departing 30 June 2026); Chief Quality Officer Hila Mory also resigned (effective 31 July 2026) and Chief Sustainability/Strategic Projects Director Charles Fergusson is departing 22 May 2026; Acting CEO Leon Fung and Chair George Adams are running the recovery in the interim with no permanent CEO in place as of September 2026

financial.description: Net debt was $472.1m at 31 Jan 2026 (net debt/EBITDA of -14x given negative EBITDA), banking covenants were waived/amended multiple times (interest cover waived for Jan-2026 test date, net senior debt/EBITDA suspended to Jul-2026), and all core facilities mature 30 June 2026 alongside the $130m Bright Dairy shareholder loan due 12 July 2026; the FY26 interim accounts carry an explicit KPMG-flagged material uncertainty around going concern

Continued access to capital depends on (1) completing planned refinancing of facilities expiring 30 June 2026, and (2) Bright Dairy's 'preliminarily indicated' but not yet formally committed continued shareholder support/loan rollover - a withdrawal or delay would be existential

China/USD-denominated sales (Abbott sale proceeds in USD) and RMB-denominated funding introduce currency risk; cash flow hedge reserve swung materially over recent periods ($(34.3)m to $13.0m fair value movements)

regulatory.risk: China SAMR infant-formula registration and demand cycle
regulatory.description: Dunsandel's SAMR registration is a valuable but narrow asset; any change in China's infant-formula regulatory regime, further consolidation among China-label manufacturers, or loss/non-renewal of registration would directly hit Advanced Nutrition; broader China birth-rate decline continues to shrink the addressable infant-formula market structurally

regulatory.risk: Overseas Investment Office / Takeovers Panel scrutiny of Bright Dairy control
regulatory.description: Bright Dairy's 65.25% stake (a Chinese state-linked entity) keeps Synlait under ongoing regulatory and public-interest attention regarding foreign control of NZ dairy infrastructure and farmer milk supply

macro.description: Farmgate milk price (forecast $9.50 base + incentives = ~$9.90/kgMS for the 2025/26 season) directly drives Synlait's largest cost line while WMP/dairy commodity global pricing (which fell sharply into late 2025) drives Ingredients segment revenue - a margin squeeze from both sides is the core cyclicality risk

With Bright Dairy (65.25%) and a2 Milk (19.83%) holding roughly 85% of shares on issue (603.2m shares), free float and trading liquidity are thin, single-stock volatility is high (52-week range roughly NZ$0.35-0.85), and minority shareholders have limited influence over strategic decisions (e.g., North Island sale, any future related-party dealings with Bright Dairy)

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global dairy ingredient and infant-formula markets are mature-to-declining in China (falling birth rates) but still support demand for premium, traceable, China-label formula; NZ processing capacity is in a period of consolidation (Westland/Yili, Miraka, Mataura Valley/a2 Milk ownership changes) as smaller processors struggle with scale economics against Fonterra
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - milk price, global WMP/dairy commodity pricing, and infant-formula demand in China all move independently and can compress margins simultaneously, as occurred in HY26
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High near-term given ~$472m net debt (pre North Island sale proceeds) and reliance on syndicated bank facilities plus a related-party shareholder loan; the April 2026 Abbott sale materially reduces this by roughly halving committed bank facilities

recent_developments.event: FY2025 annual result announced alongside a binding conditional agreement to sell North Island (Pokeno) assets to Abbott for ~US$178m (~NZ$307m); FY25 underlying NPAT was a modest $0.8m profit, masking $43.5m of one-off manufacturing-related costs; Board declined to provide FY26 guidance.

Synlait and The a2 Milk Company formally ended Synlait's exclusive manufacturing/supply rights under the NPMSA (effective retrospectively from 1 Jan 2025) in exchange for a NZ$25m payment to Synlait; minimum-volume and priority-supply obligations continue.

HY26 (six months to 31 Jan 2026) result: reported Group EBITDA of $(34.7)m, Group NPAT of $(80.6)m, operating cash outflow of $183.4m, and net debt of $472.1m; company published a 'Half Year Result & Recovery Roadmap' (Stabilise, Simplify, Scale) after identifying three core issues - manufacturing plan adjustments, lower Ingredients returns, and a deferred-tax-asset review; auditor KPMG flagged a material uncertainty related to going concern.

Completed the sale of North Island assets (Pokeno manufacturing facility, Auckland blending/canning and warehouse sites) to Abbott; gross proceeds ~NZ$283.1m received (of ~NZ$307m headline, with a further ~NZ$14m holdback released over time); ~NZ$200m of proceeds applied to repay bank debt, roughly halving committed bank facilities from NZ$400m to NZ$200m.

CEO Richard Wyeth resigned after ~11 months in the role (to depart 30 June 2026); Leon Fung appointed Acting CEO; Chair George Adams temporarily assumed additional executive leadership responsibilities. Chief Quality Officer Hila Mory also resigned (last day 31 July 2026), continuing a pattern of senior executive departures.

Synlait issued a profit warning, guiding to an underlying net loss after tax for FY26 (year ended 31 July 2026) of between NZ$19m and NZ$24m, extending the HY26 loss into the full year; shares fell to a five-month low on the news.

Synlait publicly denied media reports of takeover/take-private discussions involving The a2 Milk Company and Fonterra, stating it was 'not involved in any discussions' regarding such a transaction - the speculation itself signals ongoing market perception of Synlait as a consolidation target given its asset value versus depressed market capitalisation.

guidance.as_of: 2026-08-14 trading update (most recent) and HY26 result (2026-03-23)

items.vs_prior: new guidance issued (Board had withdrawn all FY26 guidance at the Sept-2025 FY25 result and again after the HY26 result)
items.notes: First quantified full-year guidance since the recovery roadmap was announced; follows a $27.3m underlying NPAT loss and $80.6m reported NPAT loss in HY26 alone, implying continued but narrower losses in H2 aided by the North Island divestment completing 1 April 2026

items.target: $9.90/kgMS total average milk payment ($9.50 base + $0.30 incentive + $0.10 secured milk premium)
items.notes: Secured Milk Premium of $0.08/kgMS (pool-wide average) also committed for FY27 and FY28 to retain Canterbury milk supply after the North Island farm exit

Board explicitly stated at the Sept-2025 FY25 result, and reaffirmed at the HY26 result, that it will not provide full FY26 financial guidance beyond the underlying-loss range issued 14 Aug 2026, given ongoing operational volatility

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Richard Wyeth (at the HY26 result, prior to his May 2026 resignation) described the result as 'frustratingly disappointing.' Chair George Adams said the company and its stakeholders are 'hungry for positive financial performance.' Acting CEO Leon Fung, commenting on the August 2026 loss guidance, said the company is 'focused on our recovery roadmap, resetting the fundamental issues that have underpinned Synlait's poor performance.' Management frames recovery in three horizons - Stabilise (operational/quality/financial resilience), Simplify (cost-out and margin focus from existing assets), Scale (new markets/customers/products) - and has explicitly flagged that trading performance must show 'sustained improvement' before the going-concern material uncertainty is resolved.

bull_case: North Island divestment to Abbott (completed April 2026) removes a chronically loss-making, capital-intensive division, roughly halves bank facilities, and refocuses the group on the single higher-quality Dunsandel site - a genuine balance-sheet and strategic reset, not merely a review

Deep majority-owner backing from Bright Dairy (65.25%) and continued alignment from a2 Milk (19.83%) provide a funding backstop unusual for a company of this size, and Bright Dairy has 'preliminarily indicated' continued shareholder support ahead of the July 2026 loan maturity

Dairyworks and Foodservice are demonstrably growing, profitable, diversifying segments (Dairyworks +51% revenue, +22% gross profit; Foodservice swung from loss to profit) that reduce reliance on the volatile Advanced Nutrition/Ingredients mix
$422m of gross NZ tax losses (with a $93m deferred tax asset already recognised) shelter future profits from tax once trading normalises, providing an earnings tailwind on any real recovery

Persistent takeover/consolidation speculation (a2 Milk/Fonterra reports denied August 2026) suggests the market perceives Synlait's underlying asset base (Dunsandel plant, SAMR registrations, milk supply) as worth more to a strategic acquirer than its current depressed market capitalisation reflects
bear_case: Going concern is not resolved: KPMG's HY26 review explicitly flags material uncertainty, all core bank facilities and the $130m Bright Dairy shareholder loan mature in mid-2026, and continued access to capital depends on both a successful refinancing and Bright Dairy support that has only been 'preliminarily indicated,' not contractually committed

Structural loss of a2 Milk's manufacturing exclusivity (ended Jan 2025) removes Synlait's strongest historic moat just as a2 Milk builds/acquires alternative NZ capacity (Mataura Valley Milk, former Yashili Pokeno plant), leaving customer concentration risk without the offsetting lock-in it used to carry

Repeated, self-inflicted manufacturing/quality execution failures (the FY25-HY26 'manufacturing plan adjustments' that drove an $80.6m HY26 net loss) show a persistent operational control problem, not simply a cyclical commodity downturn, and have now cost two CEOs and the Chief Quality Officer their jobs inside 18 months

Bright Dairy's 65.25% and a2 Milk's 19.83% stakes leave minority shareholders with a thin free float, limited governance influence, and exposure to potential related-party dealings (e.g., the proposed Dairyworks-Bright Dairy China retail partnership) that may not be struck at arm's length terms

FY26 guidance (Aug 2026) confirms a third consecutive year of underlying losses even after the North Island divestment proceeds and cost-out programme, with no permanent CEO in place and no formal FY26 EBITDA/revenue guidance offered - visibility into when (or if) sustained profitability returns remains very low
